title: Golden Dome economics - the $1.2T estimate, the 6x gap, and the SpaceX conflict
source: Public record: CBO (May 2026) estimated ~$1.2T to develop/deploy/operate a Golden-Dome-like shield over 20 years - more than 2x its own 2025 figure ($542B) and ~7x the White House's May-2025 number ($175B). Breakdown: ~$740B space-based warning/tracking + interceptors, ~$270B ground-based layers, ~$180B other (sensors/R&D); the space-based interceptor layer alone = ~70% of acquisition / ~60% of total cost. Space Force Gen. Michael Guetlein (program lead) estimated ~$185B (Mar 2026) - CBO says the gap means either a far more limited architecture or reliance on other accounts, and that no public plan exists to cost. Funding: $24.4B in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Jul 2025) + $22.5B reconciliation (Mar 2026, ~90% obligated in <6 months); FY2027 defense request a record ~$1.5T, with ~$750B earmarked for missile defense + drones + AI + industrial base. Timeline: EO (first week in office); 'operational before end of term' (Jan 2029); space interceptors targeted 2028. CBO: the system could handle multiple simultaneous missiles (hypersonic/ballistic/cruise) over CONUS+AK+HI but NOT a large-scale peer attack (Russia/China); figure is 'illustrative'. SpaceX/Starlink (~7,000 sats) is uniquely positioned for the space layer; Sen. Merkley called it 'a massive giveaway to defense contractors paid for by working Americans'. Overlay on the Golden_Dome / defense-tech / Project_Meridian threads; structural edges only (dollar figures in notes). HONESTY: CBO/WH/Pentagon numbers, funding, timeline, and capability limits = fact; the 'giveaway' line = cited critique (Merkley), labeled; the SpaceX-positioning + Musk-conflict = interpretation, labeled. No cabal.

edges.notes: CBO (May 2026): ~$1.2T over 20 years - >2x its own 2025 estimate ($542B) and ~7x the White House's May-2025 figure ($175B). Breakdown: ~$740B space (warning/tracking + interceptors), ~$270B ground layers, ~$180B other; the space-based interceptor layer = ~70% of acquisition / ~60% of total cost. CBO called it 'illustrative' and said no public plan exists to cost precisely (fact).

Space Force Gen. Michael Guetlein leads the program and estimated ~$185B (Mar 2026) - roughly 1/6 of CBO's number. CBO says the gap implies either a much more limited architecture or heavy reliance on other budget accounts. Space interceptors targeted for 2028; 'operational before end of term' (Jan 2029) (fact of the estimate + gap; which number is right = contested/unknowable without a public plan).

Funded via the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ($24.4B, Jul 2025) + a $22.5B reconciliation tranche (Mar 2026, ~90% obligated in <6 months). The FY2027 defense request is a record ~$1.5T, with ~$750B earmarked for missile defense + drones + AI + industrial base - Golden Dome anchors the topline (fact).

Legacy primes (Lockheed Martin, RTX, L3Harris) compete for the ground-interceptor + sensor layers (~$270B+) while the space layer favors new-space; the program splits spend between the old and new defense-industrial bases (fact of competition).
RTX (Raytheon) and other incumbents bid the interceptor/radar layers - the legacy-prime share of the shield (fact).

Golden Dome is the single biggest new line item feeding the venture-defense wave: the dominant SPACE layer (~70% of cost) favors SpaceX/Starlink (~7,000 sats already - a scale comparable to a limited space-based MD constellation) and new-space entrants. Sen. Merkley: 'a massive giveaway to defense contractors paid for by working Americans' (fact of the budget pull + the positioning; 'giveaway' = cited critique, labeled).

THE CONFLICT, with a dollar figure: Elon Musk co-directs the Pentagon's Project Meridian capabilities study while SpaceX is the natural prime for Golden Dome's dominant, ~$740B space-based layer. A panel co-director advising on priorities adjacent to his own firm's largest potential contract (interpretation, labeled; sharpens the revolving-door concern from the Meridian + defense-tech blocks).

FISCAL TIE: a $1.2T-over-20yr program (CBO) layered onto a record ~$1.5T annual defense request lands on the same Treasury-issuance / deficit the macro threads track - the missile shield is also a bond-supply story (interpretation, labeled; the exact Golden Dome contribution is a fraction, not the driver).
